clientKind.description: Web or native, deciding where the refresh handle goes.

fullName.description: Their name, as they want it shown.

password.description: Used only when the invited address has no account yet.

token.description: The handle from the invitation link.

oneOf.description:
Null when an existing account was linked — the client sends them to the sign-in screen.
Accepting an invitation deliberately does not mint a session for an account whose password the
holder of the link has not proven they know.

outcome.description: Whether a new account was created and signed in, or an existing one was linked to the roster.

note.description: Required. An unexplained adjustment is the one nobody can defend.

amount.description: How much of the payment goes to it.
How much of the payment went to it.

sequence.description: Its 1-based position in the plan — "the second instalment".

entries.description: The whole register in one request, not one call per member.

mark.description:
What happened. `Unmarked` is accepted and undoes a mistake — a coach who marked the wrong
row needs a way back, and the alternative is a no-show nobody can clear.

booked.description: Seats claimed and not given up.

excused.description: Absent with the studio's blessing. Credit refunded.

noShow.description: Did not, and did not cancel in time.

unmarked.description:
Still unanswered. Reported rather than folded into one of the others, because "nobody took the
register" and "nobody came" are different facts and only one of them is about the members.

AuditAction.description:
What kind of thing happened. Stored as a string, so adding one is a code change with no
migration and reading the table needs no lookup.

AuditEventSummary.description: One audit row, as another module or the API may read it.

actorStaffMemberId.description: Who. Null for a platform operator, who is on no roster — see ActorUserId.

actorUserId.description:
The account behind the actor. Present even when the staff member id is not, which is how a
platform operator's actions are attributable at all.

metadata.description: Scalars describing the change. Never content (ADR-0057's rule).

occurredAt.description: When. Also the partition key, so it is never null and never updated.

resourceId.description: Which row, when the action named one.

resourceKind.description: The table or aggregate, in `schema.table` form.

summary.description: Short machine-readable description from a closed set.

organizationId.description: The studio the session is acting in.

refreshHandle.description:
Null for web clients, whose handle went into a `HttpOnly` cookie the response body must
not duplicate — a handle in the body is a handle in script's reach, which is exactly what the
cookie flag was for.

bookedCount.description: Seats claimed after this one, straight from the claiming statement.

creditsRemaining.description:
The member's balance afterwards, or null when the membership is unlimited — where a number
would be a lie rather than a large value.

BookingState.description: A member's claim on a seat.

reason.description:
Why, in the operator's own words. CLAUDE.md §6 requires a reason; it is stored in the audit
row's metadata rather than its summary, because the summary is a closed vocabulary the trail is
queried by and free text there would make "how often is break-glass used" unanswerable.

closesAt.description: Local time. Must be after OpensAt.

isOpen.description: Whether the studio actually opens. False keeps the times for later.

opensAt.description: Local time in the organization's zone.

intervals.description: The complete week. Anything omitted is deleted.

CalendarRange.description: How far the calendar can be trusted.

from.description: First day of the answered window, in the studio's zone.

horizonThrough.description:
The furthest date generation will ever reach — today plus the 84-day horizon (ADR-0030). A
request past this is refused rather than answered emptily.

materializedThrough.description: The most important field on this record. The last date class occurrences have actually been generated through, or null when the materialiser has never run for this studio. Without it, a week past the horizon and a week the studio genuinely has nothing on are the same empty array, and the client renders "no classes" for both. One of those is a fact and the other is a job that has not run.

classDefinitionId.description: Present for class occurrences; lets the client group a series.

startsAt.description: The instant. The client formats; the server never sends a formatted date.

state.description: Scheduled, cancelled, completed or a moved tombstone.

title.description: Snapshotted at creation, never read through from the class (ADR-0035).

range.description: What window was answered, and how far generation reaches.

sessions.description: Flat and ordered by start. Grouping into days is the client's job.

followUpAt.description:
When to try again. Refused alongside `Spoke` — a call that reached the lead has nothing to
follow up, and scheduling one anyway is how a dealt-with lead stays on the call list forever.

reason.description: Why the membership was ended early.
Why it was called off. Shown to the members who lose their seat.

creditsRemaining.description: The balance afterwards, or null for an unlimited membership.

refunded.description: Whether a credit came back. False for a late member cancellation.

CatalogEntryUsage.description: What is pointing at a catalog entry, and therefore what deleting it would do.

canDelete.description: Whether an unqualified delete would succeed. False does not mean the studio is stuck — deactivating always works for a non-system entry, and reassigning then deleting works too.

isSystem.description: Whether code resolves it. A system entry is never deletable.

references.description: Per module and entity. Empty means nothing points at it.

CatalogReference.description: One module's answer to "is anything of mine pointing at this catalog entry?".

blocksDeletion.description:
Whether these rows would be orphaned by a delete.
            Not every reference does. Historical rows — a stage transition, a delivered gift — record what
was true at the time and keep rendering from their own stored copy of the name, so deleting the
entry loses nothing. Live references — a member's interest, a class's category — would be left
pointing at nothing.

count.description: How many rows. Zero is a valid answer and means "not mine".

entity.description:
The referencing entity, e.g. `Member`. A module may reference one catalog from several
entities — leads reference a stage from both the lead and its transition history — and the
counts have to stay distinguishable, because one of them blocks deletion and one does not.

module.description:
The owning module, e.g. `Members`. Returned to the client so the conflict dialog can say
which screen to go and look at.

giftTemplates.description: What a studio gives away, with structured effects.

interests.description: What leads and members are interested in.

leadStages.description: The pipeline board's columns, in board order.

packageTemplates.description: Sellable membership shapes. Prices omitted per permission.

currentPassword.description: Proof the caller is the account holder rather than a stolen access token.

newPassword.description: The replacement. Checked against the policy.

defaultCapacity.description: Positive. Copied onto each occurrence at materialisation.

anchorDate.description: The first occurrence. Sets the phase; immutable once set.

capacity.description: Seats on the occurrences it produces.

coachStaffMemberId.description: The effective coach: this slot's own, or the class's default where the slot names none. Reporting the stored value would leave the column blank for every slot that simply inherits — which is most of them — and the timetable screen would show a studio whose classes nobody teaches. This is also the value the materialiser stamps onto each occurrence, so the timetable and the calendar agree about who is teaching.

startsAtLocal.description: Wall-clock time in the studio's zone. Never an instant (ADR-0030).

validTo.description: Exclusive end, or null for indefinitely.

isActive.description: Whether the class is offered for new scheduling.

isActive.description: Whether it is offered for new scheduling.

slots.description: When it runs. Ordered by weekday then time.

reason.description: Which bucket. A closed set, because these are what a studio acts on.

oneOf.description: Where the conversation happened. Defaults to WhatsApp.

year.description: Which month the delivery is about. Null for the studio's month.

format.description:

memberId.description: One member, when the export was asked for from their drawer.

rowCount.description: How many rows the file has, or will have.

kind.description: A consultation or a trial class.

expiring.description: Active and ending within the renewal window.

freezes.description: Every freeze on the current membership.

recentSessions.description: The last page of ledger rows.

packageName.description: What they are on, snapshotted at sale (ADR-0035). Null with no membership.

large value.

sessionsTotal.description: Everything ever credited, so "8 of 10" renders without the ledger.

revision.description: Increments on every save. What a delivery points at.

weeks.description: Only the weeks that were written, ascending.

classDefinitionId.description: Optional, when the one-off belongs to a class's series.

permissions.description: What they may do. Advisory — every one is re-checked on the request that uses it.

PlatformTokens.description: What a successful platform sign-in hands back.

accessToken.description: Short-lived bearer token on the `fitbase-admin` audience.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working. There is nothing to renew it with.

operatorId.description: The grant this token acts under.

permissions.description:
The platform permissions the operator holds, for the client to shape its own navigation.
Advisory: every one is re-checked server-side on the request that uses it.

weeks.description: The whole month. What is sent is what exists afterwards.

year.description: Four digits, or null with Month for the studio's month.

ProgramCounters.description: What the month looks like across the roster.

delivered.description: How many have been passed on at least once. Counts self-reported deliveries, and the response says so through each row's evidence — this is the studio's working number, not the delivery-rate metric ADR-0054 excludes them from.

members.description: How many members are in scope.

withProgram.description: How many have at least one week written.

ProgramDeliveryChannel.description: How a programme reached the member.

ProgramDeliveryRecord.description: A record that a programme was passed to the member.

channel.description: Where to look for the conversation.

deliveredAt.description: When. UTC; the client renders it in the studio's zone.

evidence.description:
How it is known. `SelfReported` is a coach's assertion and is excluded from every
delivery-rate metric (ADR-0054) — the client shows "kendisi bildirdi" so the exclusion is
visible where the claim is.

programRevision.description: The programme revision this delivery was made against.

ProgramRoster.description: The programme screen for one month.

counters.description: The three numbers above the list, over the same set of rows.

isCurrentMonth.description:
Whether ProgramMonth ProgramRoster.Month is the studio's current month, decided in the organization's zone.
The client cannot decide this: the device clock is in whichever zone the laptop is in.

items.description: One line per member, by name.

month.description: The month these rows are about.

scope.description:
`Own` when the rows are the caller's assigned members, `All` for the whole
        organization. Server-computed from the caller's permission, never requested.

ProgramRosterEntry.description: One line of the programme screen: a member, and where their month stands.

phoneNumber.description: Digits as the studio typed them, or null. What the client opens a conversation with — and nothing more: the `wa.me` link carries no `text` parameter (ADR-0054).

primaryCoachStaffMemberId.description:
Who the member is assigned to. Present so a manager's oversight view can group by coach without
asking the members module a second time.

revision.description: The programme's revision, or null when there is no programme.

weeksWritten.description: How many weeks have a plan. Zero means nothing has been written.

plan.description: What the member does. Empty is not stored — the week is simply absent.

weekNumber.description: 1–6. Six is how many calendar weeks a month can touch.

plan.description: Blank deletes the week rather than storing an empty one.

weekNumber.description: 1–6. Six is how many calendar weeks a month can touch.

ReceivableItem.description: One thing a studio is owed.

daysOverdue.description: Zero when it is not. How late, in whole days past the grace period.

dueOn.description: The organization-local date it fell due.

isOverdue.description:
Computed from the studio's today and its own grace period, at read time. Server-computed because
the client's "today" is whatever zone the laptop is in.

outstandingAmount.description: What is left after allocations from payments that were not voided. The number that makes partial payment expressible — ₺1,400 of a ₺2,400 instalment, which the panel's single amount column cannot say.

status.description:
Where it is in its life. On the receivables list this is always `Pending`; on a plan's
instalments it is what separates one that was paid from one the studio wrote off. Without it
those two are both "outstanding 0.00" and read as the same thing, which they are not — a
cancelled instalment is a discount the studio gave.

overdueGraceDays.description: Days past due before an unpaid installment reads as late. 0–90; seven by default.

ReceivablesList.description: What a studio is owed, and how much of it is late.

cursor.description: Keyset continuation, or null at the end.

graceDays.description:
The number the answer was computed with. Returned so the screen can say "7 günden fazla gecikmiş"
rather than making the client guess, and so a support question about a surprising row has an
answer in the response itself.

items.description: Oldest due date first — the order somebody chases in.

overdueCount.description: How many instalments, which the sum alone does not say.

totalOverdue.description: The part past its grace period.

ReceivablesPolicy.description: When the studio starts chasing money it is owed.

overdueGraceDays.description:
Days past `due_on` before an unpaid installment counts as overdue. Seven by default (plan
decision D10); zero means the day after it falls due.

refreshHandle.description: Native clients only; web clients send the cookie.

amount.description: How much goes back. May be part of the payment.

note.description: Free text, and personal data — a refund note routinely explains a health reason.

reason.description: The closed vocabulary the report groups by.

acceptedKvkkNotice.description: Whether the aydınlatma metni was acknowledged.

clientKind.description: Web or native, deciding where the refresh handle goes.

password.description: Checked against the policy before anything is written.

orderedEntryIds.description: Every entry in the catalog, exactly once, in the new order.

password.description: The new password. Checked against the policy.

token.description: The handle from the reset link.

priceOverride.description: What was actually charged, when it differs from the template.

creditsRefunded.description:
How many got a credit back. Lower than SeatsReleased when some of the
bookings were on unlimited memberships, which consume nothing and so refund nothing.

seatsReleased.description: How many members lost their seat.

SessionClientKind.description: Where a session is being used from. Decides how the refresh handle is carried.

SessionDetail.description: One session with its register. Serves the calendar drawer and the attendance sheet.

attendance.description: The counts, computed from Seats by the same rules the mark endpoint returns.

notes.description: Free text the studio put on it.

seats.description:
Every booking ever made on this session, cancelled ones included. The register renders the live
ones; the cancelled ones are what answers "who dropped out" without a second query.

SessionKind.description: What a session is. One table holds all three (ADR-0032).

balanceAfter.description: The balance immediately after, so the history reads without re-summing.

attendance.description: Whether they turned up. `Unmarked` until somebody says.

memberName.description:
Resolved through `IMemberDirectory`. Null when the id resolves to nothing — a member
deleted under an erasure request. Rendered as unknown rather than refusing to open the register.

state.description: Booked or cancelled. A cancelled seat stays on the sheet as evidence.

SessionState.description: Where a session is in its life.

coachStaffMemberId.description: Null takes the class's default coach.

startsAtLocal.description:
Wall-clock time in the studio's zone, and it stays one. "09:00 Tuesday" means 09:00 in March and
09:00 in November; sending an instant would move it by an hour twice a year (ADR-0030).

validFrom.description: First day. Defaults to the studio's today. The anchor is derived from it.

validTo.description: Exclusive end, or null for indefinitely.

StaffMemberSummary.description: What other modules may know about a staff member.

fullName.description: Display name. Personal data; declared in the register.

id.description: The assignment key. Every `*_staff_member_id` column in every module points here — not at a user id, because a staff member can exist before their account does (ADR-0016).

StaffRole.description: A role held by a staff member within an organization.

StaffStatus.description: A staff member's state on the roster.

SupportAuditEvent.description: One break-glass event, with the studio it was opened against.

organizationId.description: Which studio. Never null for this action.

SupportOrganizationSnapshot.description: What a break-glass session reads about one studio.

deletionRequestedAt.description: When deletion was requested, or null.

SupportStaffMember.description: One roster row, as a support session sees it.

email.description: Their address, which is how a support conversation identifies them.

isOwner.description: Whether they are the studio's owner.

role.description: Their role, as a wire enum name.

userId.description: Their account, or null if they have not accepted an invitation yet.

taxIdentifier.description: VKN or TCKN. Null leaves the stored one alone, so a form that never displays it can save the other fields; an empty string clears it.

TaxProfileSummary.description: The tax profile, with the identifier redacted.

certificateObjectKey.description: Object-storage key of the uploaded certificate.

hasTaxIdentifier.description: Whether one is stored at all, which the digits alone cannot say.

taxIdentifierLastDigits.description: The last two digits, so somebody can confirm the right number is stored. The full identifier is never returned — it is special-category data under KVKK and the screen does not need it to render.

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn. "İki kere girildi".

Minted only by the admin sign-in flow, which requires a password and a TOTP code, and accepted only under `/api/v1/admin`.
